title: Meta-RAG Code Summarization for Large-Scale Migrations
problem: Large codebases exceed context windows; agents can't reason about 1M+ LOC projects in one pass

title: Structural codebase optimization for agent reasoning efficiency
problem: Agent reasoning degrades on codebases designed for humans; scattered symbols, deep nesting, and missing indices force agents to waste tokens on navigation and rediscovery

title: Controlled Dead Code Removal with Language-Specific Linters
problem: Dead code accumulates; removing it without false positives requires careful tooling and verification

title: Hybrid Codemod + Agent Approach for Large-Scale Refactoring
problem: Pure agent approaches burn tokens/cost on repetitive file edits; pure codemods lack contextual reasoning

title: Phased Dependency Upgrades Across Large Codebases
problem: Major dependency upgrades cause cascading failures; undisciplined agent upgrades break production

title: Structured Workflow for Safe Monolith Decomposition
problem: Decomposing monoliths is high-risk; undisciplined refactoring causes hidden breakages

title: Subagent Orchestration for Bulk Test Generation
problem: Single agent degrades in quality over many iterations on large codebases; test generation stalls

title: Agent context as a managed lifecycle with validation
problem: Agent conversations accumulate context (turns, tool outputs, intermediate facts) with token cost growing quadratically; naive summarization compresses linearly but produces accuracy cliffs. Context needs staged management with fidelity validation.

title: Agentic RAG with tool-based on-demand retrieval over vector search
problem: Pre-computed vector embeddings don't scale to evolving codebases; large corpus RAG adds retrieval latency; traditional RAG can ground answers in incorrect documents

title: Auto memory for persistent learning across Claude Code sessions
problem: Claude forgets learnings across sessions (build commands, debugging patterns, test quirks); repeated discoveries waste tokens and time

title: Managing Claude Code's context window for long sessions
problem: Sessions accumulate context (files, CLAUDE.md, memory, tool output) and eventually approach limits; poor management wastes tokens or forces suboptimal trade-offs between scope and precision

title: CLAUDE.md files for persistent session memory
problem: Each Claude Code session starts with empty context; repeating instructions, conventions, and project knowledge wastes tokens and causes Claude to re-learn the same patterns

title: Context compaction for long-running agent sessions
problem: Long conversations and multi-turn agentic loops accumulate history that pushes toward context window limits; users can't continue without manual intervention

title: Filesystem as primary context layer for agents
problem: Putting all context in the prompt creates token overhead, makes just-in-time discovery difficult, and scatters state across sessions

title: Lost-in-middle mitigation — reordering context to preserve attention on critical tokens
problem: Models lose focus on tokens in the middle of long contexts (U-shaped attention curve); critical information buried in the middle of 50K+ token contexts gets overlooked

title: Use code APIs instead of tool definitions for MCP servers
problem: Loading all MCP tool definitions upfront consumes 25-72% of context window before any real work; agents need progressive disclosure of capabilities

title: Progressive disclosure — load context names first, full content on demand
problem: Loading all context upfront (all skill definitions, complete tool schemas, full documentation) wastes tokens on content agents may never use

title: Prompt caching to reduce API costs and latency
problem: Long, repetitive prompts (system instructions, large contexts) re-sent on every request waste tokens and latency

title: Action caching and deterministic replay for agent debugging and cost analysis
problem: Agents exhibit non-deterministic behavior across runs; same prompt + context can yield different tool calls, making bugs hard to isolate and cost attribution impossible

title: Adversarial code review with fresh-context verifier agents
problem: Agents cannot reliably review their own code; same-context verification misses bugs

title: Preventing Claude from inventing non-existent APIs
problem: Claude generates code calling methods that don't exist, especially for unfamiliar libraries

title: Tiered LLM-as-judge architecture for cost-efficient code evaluation
problem: Single-model judges are expensive at scale; need cost-effective frontline filtering

title: Mutation testing to verify AI-generated test quality
problem: AI-generated tests reach high coverage but have weak assertions; mutations expose gaps

title: Schema validation and deterministic checks as first-line verification gates
problem: Many hallucinations can be caught mechanically before running LLM judges without expensive inference

title: Self-critique reflection loops for agent code generation
problem: First-draft agent output often has fixable errors; iteration improves quality

title: Antigravity Agent Manager for multi-agent orchestration
problem: Running multiple agents in parallel requires manual coordination; no unified view of progress or async task delegation

title: Claude ↔ Antigravity task handoff
problem: You use both Claude Code and Antigravity CLI, but work and context don't flow between them, so you re-explain the task in each.

title: Claude Code as an MCP server (exposing tools to other agents)
problem: Other agents can't access Claude Code's capabilities (file editing, bash, codebase search) directly

title: MCP Applications for structured agent task automation
problem: Simple tool calls don't capture rich agent workflows; MCP Apps provides semantics for multi-step tasks, async execution, and agent communication

title: MCP as the universal integration layer for agent tooling
problem: Every agent needs custom integrations to each tool; MCP standardizes how agents talk to external systems

title: Shared context file (HANDOFF.md) for agent state passing
problem: Sequential agents lack shared state; context is lost or re-explained on each session

title: Agent Teams for parallel peer coordination
problem: Subagents work in isolation with parent-child messaging only; need peer-to-peer coordination between agents on same codebase.

title: Cost-aware model routing with hard budget caps
problem: Unbounded agent execution wastes budget on overkill model choices; teams need runtime cost control to degrade gracefully or route to cheaper models when approaching limits

title: Debate pattern for multi-perspective verification
problem: Single agent review misses classes of issues (security, performance, tests); need independent perspectives on same code.

title: Git worktree per-agent isolation for parallel development
problem: Multiple agents on same branch collide on file writes; need per-agent isolated working directories.

title: MCP for standardized tool coordination across agents
problem: Each agent reimplements tool integrations; need standardized, reusable tool interface across agent network.

title: Planner-executor loop for iterative code generation
problem: Large code-generation tasks fail when agent tries to write and test in a single pass; need separate planning and execution phases.

title: Sub-agent fan-out for parallel exploration & review
problem: A single agent's context fills up and serializes work that is naturally parallel (searching many files, reviewing many dimensions).

title: Supervisor pattern for hierarchical task decomposition
problem: Complex tasks overwhelm a single agent's context; need centralized task decomposition with specialized workers.

title: Few-shot examples anchor format and behavior
problem: Instructions alone don't reliably guide output format, tone, or edge-case handling

title: Instruction hierarchy across CLAUDE.md, system prompt, and skills
problem: Conflicting or scattered instructions cause agent behavior inconsistency

title: When negative instructions work (and when they fail)
problem: "Do not" instructions sometimes work, sometimes fail to prevent unwanted behavior

title: Path-scoped rules for directory and file-type instructions
problem: Large CLAUDE.md files consume tokens in every session; rules should load only when relevant to current work

title: Structured outputs for guaranteed schema compliance
problem: Prompt-only JSON constraints allow malformed output, invalid fields, type errors

title: XML tags for unambiguous prompt structure
problem: Long prompts mixing instructions, context, examples, and inputs cause misinterpretation

title: Building Custom Subagents for Focused Tasks
problem: Large tasks flood main context with exploration noise; subagents preserve context by delegating focused work.

title: Claude Code Hooks for Tool Automation and Control
problem: Manual tool governance is tedious; hooks automate enforcement, formatting, and safety gates without blocking workflow.

title: Tool Naming and Descriptions for Accurate Agent Routing
problem: Ambiguous tool names and vague descriptions cause agents to misroute, pick wrong tools, or waste tokens deciding.

title: MCP Error Handling for Model Self-Correction
problem: Unhandled tool errors crash agents; structured errors enable models to recover intelligently.

title: Designing MCP Tools for Agent Clarity and Composability
problem: Poorly designed tools confuse agents and waste context through unclear purposes and fragmented operations.

title: Sandboxing MCP Tool Execution for Security and Isolation
problem: Running untrusted tool code in the MCP server process enables code injection, resource exhaustion, and lateral movement.

title: Test-Driven Development with AI agents
problem: AI agents skip tests or write tests that don't capture requirements, leading to false-passing code

title: Checkpoint and commit discipline for agent-written code
problem: When agents produce large changes without commits, bugs become hard to isolate and recovery is painful

title: Explore-Plan-Code-Commit workflow for agent tasks
problem: Ad-hoc agent direction produces inconsistent results and wasted exploration

title: Strategic human-in-the-loop review gates
problem: Too few gates = unsafe agent autonomy; too many gates = bottleneck that defeats the point

title: Iterative self-refinement loops for agent code quality
problem: Agents produce code on first try that is correct but unmaintainable, or that misses edge cases

title: Plan-then-Execute pattern for structured agent workflows
problem: Agents executing without a plan produce meandering, error-prone changes and waste compute

title: Spec-driven development with agent coding
problem: Agents without a spec drift into scope creep, build the wrong thing, or make incompatible changes
